assign.outcome:
**Deliverable 8 shipped: a VS Code tab is now an agent you can message.** `register_session({id, session_id})` (new `Servex/agents/External.js`) makes any Claude session Servex did not spawn addressable: `list_agents` shows it (`kind: "external"`), `send_to_agent` appends to its own inbox file (`logs/inbox/<id>.jsonl`) instead of throwing, and the owner's words on any card it creates are forwarded there too — a small, code-only module installed the same way `Layers.js` and `Cards.js` are, one line in `Servex.js`.

Proved on a private Servex (port 8490, `SERVEX_NO_LAYERS=1` per the brief): a card message reaches the tab's inbox in single-digit milliseconds, far under the 2-second bar. 9/9 unit checks pass against a real `Agents` host.

Caught and closed along the way: a test-only bug that briefly wrote real lines into the live Servex's home directory (ES module import hoisting beat a `process.env.SERVEX_HOME` override) — found, cleaned up, and fixed before landing, with the mechanism written up so it doesn't recur. Also hit and recovered from a shared-worktree race where a sibling minion's concurrent edit silently dropped mine from `Agents.js`/`Servex.js`; re-applied and committed promptly.

Left open, and why: `Agents.revive()` (outside this task's send-path-only fence) doesn't yet know how to tell an external row apart from a dead one across a Servex restart — it buries it `gone`, and a fresh `register_session` call restores it. `readme.md` wasn't updated (not in the file fence).
